page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes a local 33 GB SSD and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 2707.07, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 5410.95 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3600.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations also fall into the lower performance tiers.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4as_v4 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the premium cost of memory-optimized or compute-optimized tiers. Given the strong single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, this server is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic application hosting, single-threaded processing tasks, and development or testing environments that do not demand high parallel throughput.
